eyebrow: Friction doesn't stop the work -- it redirects it

steps.label: Shared credentials
steps.sub: approval is too slow, so one login gets passed around -- zero accountability

steps.label: Shadow exports
steps.sub: ACLs are too narrow, so data leaves the platform into a personal file

steps.label: Shadow IT
steps.sub: the workflow is too locked down, so a team builds its own ungoverned tool

eyebrow: The failure mode, in one comparison
code:
Restrictive policy intended to prevent:     What it actually produces:
One person seeing too much data        ->  No individual sees it with any audit trail
Data leaving via an approved export     ->  Data leaving via an unaudited spreadsheet
An unmanaged workflow                   ->  A fully unmanaged outside tool
caption: Each workaround is strictly less secure than what it replaced.

steps.label: High-risk access
steps.sub: approval-chain overrides, regulated data -- friction earns its keep

steps.label: Everyday access
steps.sub: as frictionless as the actual risk tolerates, not maximally locked

steps.label: Uniform restriction fails
steps.sub: it looks secure on an audit checklist, performs badly in practice
